L4.t: Listening · Part 4: A talk about sleep
L4.x:
Many people believe that they can manage perfectly well on five or six hours of sleep a night. However, research suggests that most adults need between seven and nine hours to stay healthy.
During sleep, the brain organises the information we have learned during the day. That is why students who sleep well before an exam often remember more than those who stay up all night studying.
One of the biggest enemies of good sleep is the light from phone and computer screens. This light tells the brain that it is still daytime. Experts recommend switching off screens at least one hour before going to bed and keeping the bedroom cool, dark and quiet.

L5.x:
Interviewer: So, Malika, why would you like to work in our hotel?
Malika: Well, I've always enjoyed meeting people from different countries. I studied tourism at college, and last summer I worked as a receptionist at a small guest house in Bukhara.
Interviewer: That's useful experience. What did you find most difficult there?
Malika: At first, dealing with complaints. Some guests were angry when things went wrong. But I learned to stay calm, listen carefully and find a solution.
Interviewer: Good. This job sometimes includes night shifts. Is that a problem for you?
Malika: Not at all. I live quite close, only ten minutes away by bus.
Interviewer: Excellent. And which languages do you speak?
Malika: Uzbek and Russian, of course, and English. I'm also learning Turkish at the moment.

L6.t: Listening · Part 6: Radio report on cycling
L6.x:
More and more people in our city are choosing to cycle to work. According to a recent survey, the number of daily cyclists has doubled in the last three years.
The main reason people give is health: cycling is an easy way to include exercise in a busy day. Others say they save money on fuel and public transport. Some simply enjoy avoiding traffic jams.
However, cyclists also have complaints. The most common one is the lack of safe bicycle lanes on major roads. The city council has promised to build forty kilometres of new lanes by the end of next year, starting with the streets around the university.

R1.t: Reading · Text 1: The camel of the desert
R1.x:
The camel is perfectly adapted to life in the desert. Contrary to popular belief, a camel's hump does not store water. Instead, it stores fat, which the animal can use as a source of energy when food is scarce. When the fat is used up, the hump becomes smaller and may even fall to one side.
Camels can go for a week or more without drinking, and when they find water they can drink more than one hundred litres in a few minutes. Their bodies lose very little water: they hardly sweat, and their body temperature can rise by several degrees during the day before they start to lose moisture.
Other features also help camels survive. Long eyelashes and nostrils that can close protect them from sand storms, and wide, thick feet stop them sinking into the sand. For thousands of years, these remarkable animals have carried people and goods across the deserts of Asia and Africa.

R2.t: Reading · Text 2: Learning a language online
R2.x:
Ten years ago, a student who wanted to learn a foreign language usually had to join a class or hire a private teacher. Today, thousands of apps and websites promise to make the process faster, cheaper and more enjoyable.
Supporters of online learning point out that it is flexible. Learners can practise whenever they have a few free minutes – on the bus, during a lunch break or before going to sleep. Many apps also turn learning into a game, giving points and rewards that keep users motivated.
Critics, however, argue that apps are good for vocabulary but weak at developing real communication skills. Speaking a language means reacting quickly to another person, and a phone cannot fully replace a live conversation. Most experts therefore suggest a mixture: use technology for regular practice, but find opportunities to speak with real people as often as possible.

R3.t: Reading · Text 3: The history of tea
R3.x:
According to a Chinese legend, tea was discovered almost five thousand years ago, when some leaves fell into a pot of boiling water that was being prepared for the emperor. Whether or not this story is true, tea has been drunk in China for many centuries.
From China, tea spread along trade routes to Central Asia, the Middle East and eventually Europe. It arrived in Europe in the seventeenth century and was at first so expensive that only rich families could afford it. Tea was often kept in locked boxes, and the key was held by the lady of the house.
Over time, prices fell and tea became the everyday drink of millions. In Central Asia, the teahouse, or choyxona, became an important place where men met to talk, relax and discuss local news. Even today, offering a bowl of tea is a sign of hospitality in many Uzbek homes.

R4.x:
Volunteering means giving your time and skills to help others without being paid. Volunteers work in hospitals, schools, animal shelters, parks and at large events such as sports competitions.
While the main purpose of volunteering is to help the community, volunteers themselves often benefit too. Studies show that people who volunteer regularly feel less stressed and more satisfied with their lives. Young volunteers also gain practical experience that can be useful when they apply for jobs or university places.
Not everyone has a lot of free time, but even a few hours a month can make a difference. Organisations usually provide training, so volunteers do not need special qualifications to start. What matters most is reliability: an organisation must be able to count on its volunteers to arrive when they have promised.

R5.t: Reading · Text 5: Plastic in the oceans
R5.x:
Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic end up in the world's oceans. Some of it comes from ships, but most is carried from land by rivers and the wind. Because plastic breaks down extremely slowly, a single bottle can remain in the sea for hundreds of years.
Over time, sunlight and waves break plastic into tiny pieces called microplastics. These are eaten by fish and other sea creatures, and they can eventually enter the human food chain. Scientists are still studying how dangerous this is for our health.
There are reasons for hope, however. Many countries have banned or taxed plastic bags, and some companies are developing packaging made from plants. Individuals can also help by carrying reusable bags and bottles and by recycling correctly. As one researcher put it, "The best way to clean the ocean is to stop the plastic reaching it in the first place."

wr.title: A message to a friend
wr.sit: Your friend Sam is visiting Tashkent next week and has asked you for advice about what to do there.
wr.ins: Write a short message to Sam (about 50 words). Suggest two places to visit and say why you recommend them.
tips: Do'stona salomlashish bilan boshlang: Hi Sam!
Ikkita joyni nomlang va har biriga sabab yozing
Qisqa, norasmiy jumlalar ishlating (I think, you'll love...)
Xayrlashuv bilan tugating: See you soon!
wr.sample:
Hi Sam!
I'm so happy you're coming! You should definitely visit Chorsu Bazaar – it's the best place to try local bread and fruit. Also, take the metro: every station looks like a museum. Let me know your dates and we can meet up.
See you soon,
Aziz

wr.title: Thanking a friend
wr.sit: Your friend helped you move to a new flat last weekend.
wr.ins: Write a short message (about 50 words) to thank your friend. Say how the new flat is and invite them for dinner.
tips: Minnatdorchilikni aniq bildiring: Thanks a lot for...
Yangi kvartira haqida 1–2 jumla yozing
Taklifni aniq vaqt bilan bering
Hajm 50 so'z atrofida bo'lsin
wr.sample:
Hi Dilnoza,
Thanks a lot for helping me last weekend – I couldn't have done it without you! The flat is small but really bright, and the neighbours are friendly. Would you like to come for dinner on Friday at seven? I'll cook plov!
Love,
Madina

wr.title: A complaint to an online shop
wr.sit: You ordered a pair of headphones from an online shop. They arrived two weeks late and one side does not work.
wr.ins: Write a letter to the shop manager (120–150 words). Explain the problem, say how you felt and what you would like the shop to do.
tips: Rasmiy murojaat: Dear Sir or Madam,
1-xatboshi: xat maqsadi; 2-xatboshi: muammo tafsilotlari; 3-xatboshi: talabingiz
Qisqartmalarsiz yozing: I am, I would (I'm emas)
Rasmiy yakun: Yours faithfully, + ism-familiya
wr.sample:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to complain about an order I placed on your website on 3 May (order number 4521).
According to your website, the headphones should have arrived within three days. However, they were delivered two weeks late. Moreover, when I tried them, I discovered that the left side does not work at all. As I bought them for an important online course, I was extremely disappointed and had to borrow a pair from a friend.
I would therefore be grateful if you could either send me a replacement immediately or refund the full price, including the delivery cost. I have attached a photograph of the product and the receipt.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours faithfully,
Aziz Karimov

wr.title: Applying for a volunteer position
wr.sit: A local library is looking for young volunteers to help with a summer reading programme for children.
wr.ins: Write a letter to the library director (120–150 words). Introduce yourself, explain why you are interested and describe any relevant experience.
tips: Kimligingiz va nima uchun yozayotganingizni birinchi xatboshida ayting
Tajriba va fazilatlaringizni misol bilan ko'rsating
Qachon ishlay olishingizni yozing
Yours sincerely – agar qabul qiluvchining ismini bilsangiz
wr.sample:
Dear Mrs Rahimova,
I am writing to apply for the volunteer position in your summer reading programme, which I saw advertised on the library's website.
I am a seventeen-year-old student at School No. 12, and I have always loved books. Last year I helped my younger cousins with their reading every weekend, and I noticed how quickly children become interested when stories are read aloud with enthusiasm.
I am patient, reliable and good at organising activities. I would also be happy to help with simple games or drawing tasks related to the books.
I am available every weekday morning from June to August.
Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to hearing from you.
Yours sincerely,
Lola Usmonova

wr.title: Online learning vs. classroom learning
wr.sit: Some people believe that online lessons are as effective as traditional classroom lessons. Others think nothing can replace a real teacher in a classroom.
wr.ins: Write an essay (180–200 words). Discuss both views and give your own opinion with reasons and examples.
tips: Kirish: mavzuni o'z so'zlaringiz bilan qayta ifodalang
2-xatboshi: birinchi fikr va misol; 3-xatboshi: ikkinchi fikr va misol
Bog'lovchilar: On the one hand, However, Moreover, In conclusion
Xulosada o'z fikringizni aniq bildiring
wr.sample:
Nowadays, many students take at least some of their lessons online. While some people think this is just as effective as studying in a classroom, others disagree.
On the one hand, online learning has clear advantages. Students can study at their own pace, watch recorded lessons again and avoid long journeys to school. For example, a learner living in a small village can now attend lessons given by excellent teachers in the capital.
On the other hand, a classroom offers things that a screen cannot. Teachers can immediately see when a student is confused, and pupils learn a great deal from discussing ideas with each other. Moreover, many young people find it difficult to stay focused at home, where phones and social media are a constant distraction.
In my opinion, the best approach is a combination of the two. Online tools are excellent for extra practice and for students who live far away, but regular face-to-face lessons remain essential for motivation and communication skills.
In conclusion, online learning is a valuable addition to traditional education rather than a complete replacement for it.

wr.title: Should young people work while studying?
wr.sit: More and more students have part-time jobs while they are at school or university.
wr.ins: Write an essay (180–200 words). What are the advantages and disadvantages of this? Give your opinion.
tips: Ijobiy va salbiy tomonlarni alohida xatboshilarda yozing
Har bir fikrni misol bilan mustahkamlang
Takrorlanmaslik uchun sinonimlardan foydalaning
Hajmni 180–200 so'z oralig'ida saqlang
wr.sample:
In many countries, it has become common for students to combine their studies with a part-time job. This trend has both benefits and drawbacks.
The main advantage is that working teaches young people responsibility and the value of money. A student who earns his own pocket money usually spends it more carefully. In addition, part-time jobs give valuable experience that employers appreciate. For instance, working in a café develops communication skills and the ability to stay calm under pressure.
However, there are also serious disadvantages. Students who work long hours may not have enough time or energy to study, and their marks may suffer as a result. Furthermore, they might miss important opportunities such as sports, clubs or simply time with friends and family.
In my view, a part-time job can be very useful as long as it does not take up too much time. Ten hours a week, especially during holidays, is a reasonable limit.
To sum up, working while studying can help young people mature, but education should always remain their first priority.

q: What do you usually do at the weekend?
Who do you usually spend it with?
tips: 2–3 jumlada javob bering, faqat «yes/no» demang
Sababini qo'shing: because..., so...
sp.sample: At the weekend I usually relax at home on Saturday morning and then meet my friends in the afternoon. We often play football in the park because it's a great way to stay active. On Sundays I spend time with my family – we often visit my grandparents.

q: Do you prefer reading books or watching films? Why?
tips: Tanlovingizni ayting va ikki sabab keltiring
Misol sifatida yaqinda o'qigan kitob yoki ko'rgan filmingizni tilga oling
sp.sample: I prefer reading books, to be honest. When I read, I can imagine the characters and places in my own way, and I can stop and think whenever I want. For example, I recently read a novel about the Silk Road and I enjoyed it much more than the film version.

q: What kind of music do you like?
Has your taste in music changed over the years?
tips: Present Perfect bilan o'zgarishni ifodalang: My taste has changed...
Qisqa misol keltiring
sp.sample: I like many kinds of music, but mostly pop and traditional Uzbek songs. My taste has definitely changed: when I was a child I only listened to cartoon songs, but now I enjoy more serious music, especially when I study.

q: Imagine two pictures: one shows a family having dinner together at home, the other shows people eating quickly in a fast-food restaurant.
What are the similarities and differences? Which do you prefer?
tips: Avval o'xshashlikni ayting: Both pictures show...
Keyin farqlarni: In the first picture..., whereas in the second...
Oxirida o'z afzalligingizni ayting
sp.sample: Both pictures show people having a meal. In the first picture, a family is sitting around the table at home and seems relaxed – they are probably talking about their day. In the second picture, by contrast, people are eating quickly in a fast-food restaurant, maybe because they are busy. Personally, I prefer family dinners because the food is healthier and it's a chance to talk.

q: Describe a place in Uzbekistan you would recommend to a tourist.
Say where it is, what visitors can do there and why you recommend it.
tips: 1 daqiqada reja tuzing: joy – nima qilish mumkin – nima uchun
Hikoyani ketma-ket bog'lang: First, Also, Finally
Shaxsiy tajriba qo'shing
sp.sample: I would recommend Khiva, a small city in the Khorezm region. The old part of the city, called Ichan Kala, is surrounded by thick walls and is full of mosques, madrasas and minarets. Visitors can walk through its narrow streets, climb the Islam Khodja minaret to see the whole city, and buy handmade souvenirs from local craftsmen. I visited Khiva with my family two years ago and felt as if I had travelled back in time. In the evening, the walls are lit up and the atmosphere is magical. I recommend it because it shows the history of our country in a very real way, and the people there are extremely hospitable.

q: Talk about a skill you would like to learn in the future.
Say what it is, why you want to learn it and how you would learn it.
tips: Kelajak uchun: I would like to..., I'm planning to...
Sabablarni sanab o'ting: First of all..., Another reason...
Qanday o'rganishingizni aniq ayting
sp.sample: One skill I would really like to learn is programming. First of all, technology is becoming more important in every job, so I think it will help my career. Another reason is that I enjoy solving problems, and coding is basically solving problems step by step. I'm planning to start with free online courses this summer and then join a programming club at my school. In the future, I would love to create a mobile app that helps students learn languages.

q: "Mobile phones should be banned in schools."
Discuss the arguments for and against this statement and give your opinion.
tips: Ikkala tomonni ham ayting: Some people argue that..., On the other hand...
Har biriga bittadan misol keltiring
Oxirida aniq xulosa: In my opinion...
sp.sample: This is a controversial issue. Some people argue that phones should be banned because they distract students during lessons and can lead to cheating in tests. For example, many teachers complain that pupils check social media instead of listening. On the other hand, phones can be useful learning tools: students can look up information, use dictionaries and contact their parents in an emergency. In my opinion, a complete ban is not the best solution. Instead, schools should have clear rules – for instance, phones must be switched off during lessons but can be used for educational tasks when the teacher allows it.

q: "Living in a big city is better than living in the countryside."
Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
tips: Shahar afzalliklari: ish, ta'lim, transport
Qishloq afzalliklari: toza havo, tinchlik, arzonlik
Qiyoslash so'zlari: whereas, while, compared to
sp.sample: There are strong arguments on both sides. Big cities offer more job opportunities, better universities and hospitals, and a wide choice of entertainment. Public transport also makes life convenient. However, cities can be noisy, polluted and expensive, and people often feel stressed. The countryside, by contrast, offers fresh air, peace and a strong sense of community, although there may be fewer services and jobs. Personally, I think the city is better for young people who want to study and build a career, whereas the countryside is ideal for families with small children or for people who want a calmer lifestyle.
